chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Lester Young in Alabama: the guardhouse and the picture of his wife
summary: Willard relates that Prez was jailed after a picture of his white wife was found; Collins knew only that he returned changed.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, that's -- not only that, but Lester was stationed in the South, like (inaudible).

Yeah, yeah. Oh, yeah, he was in Alabama. I knew where he was. He was not too far from where I was. I was in South Carolina. But fortunately I was with -- I was in a training camp, which means that we were there primarily to entertain the troops. We would march them in, entertain them while they're there, and we'd march them out, and bring another group in. So I stayed there for quite a while, and I had a little group there also. So I was more fortunate than Lester. I think he was in a different type of camp.

In the sketch story he says that when they searched Lester's locker they found a picture of his white wife, and this was more than his commanding officer could stand. And that this had something to do with the court martial, although efforts to find the records of what he was court marshalled for have proved fruitless. That there is no record of what he was court marshalled for, yet he was put in the guardhouse (inaudible).
For a long period of time.
Yeah, well I didn't know anything about that. Only -- I only knew that when I saw him, in New York, after the war, he had changed. There was something -- he

seemed to have lost his fire, something had happened to him. And it occurred to me that the army really did this to him because Lester was, as I said, was not emotionally up to army life. You know. That--
